title: Indeed Selects AWS as Its Preferred Cloud to Drive Efficiencies across its Global Operations
summary: Indeed has chosen Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud provider, entering a multi-year agreement to migrate over 30 petabytes of data. This move is expected to reduce Indeed's global data center footprint by 40% and streamline IT operations. By using AWS, Indeed aims to enhance its platform's availability and reliability, accelerate innovation of new customer-facing products, and leverage AWS's analytics and machine learning services to gain deeper insights into user behavior.

title: Conversation With: Danyel Surrency Jones
summary: Danyel Surrency Jones, CEO of POWERHANDZ, discusses her experiences as a Black woman entrepreneur, highlighting the challenges of proving herself in boardrooms and facing psychological biases. She shares her personal coping mechanisms, including the importance of mental health and therapy, and offers advice to business leaders on addressing racial inequities authentically, urging them to act with genuine intent rather than just following trends.

title: Gap and Etsy make millions on masks amid pandemic sales slump
summary: Gap and Etsy bolstered their pandemic-hit sales by selling millions of face masks. Gap sold $130 million worth of masks in one quarter, while Etsy's 100,000 vendors sold $346 million, accounting for 14% of the platform's total sales. Other businesses like Steele Canvas also pivoted to mask production, saving jobs and generating significant revenue.

title: Cybersquatting: Attackers Mimicking Domains of Major Brands Including Facebook, Apple, Amazon and Netflix to Scam Consumers
summary: This article discusses the widespread issue of cybersquatting, where attackers register domain names similar to major brands like Facebook, Apple, Amazon, and Netflix to scam consumers. Palo Alto Networks identified 13,857 squatting domains in December 2019 alone, with 18.59% being malicious and 36.57% posing high risks, engaging in activities such as phishing, malware distribution, and various scams. The report details different squatting techniques, common targets, and infrastructure preferences of attackers, emphasizing the need for continuous monitoring and user vigilance.

title: Home shopping's fight to stay relevant
summary: QVC and HSN are working to shed their outdated image and stay relevant in the evolving world of video shopping. They are expanding beyond traditional live TV by partnering with tech platforms, utilizing social media, and diversifying their product mix to reach new, younger audiences. While facing competition from tech giants like Amazon, QVC leverages its expertise in interactive viewing and loyal customer base.

title: Sonos wireless headphones revealed in new patent filing
summary: A new patent filing reveals Sonos' plans to enter the wireless over-ear headphone market. The patent, filed in September 2019 and recently granted, details two possible designs and innovative integration features with existing Sonos speaker systems, allowing users to "swap" audio playback between headphones and speakers. While pricing and release dates are unknown, Sonos aims to leverage its customer base with features that enhance its current audio ecosystem.

title: Walmart Takes On Amazon Prime: Membership Program Will Deliver From Stores
summary: Walmart is officially launching Walmart+, an annual membership service priced at $98 per year or $12.95 per month, to compete with Amazon Prime. The program will offer free same-day delivery of groceries and other items from local stores, gas discounts, and mobile checkout, with plans to expand perks. Walmart hopes to leverage its extensive grocery business to attract subscribers, many of whom already use Amazon Prime.

title: Trace the Journey of Your Coffee from Crop to Cup with Ethical Bean
summary: Ethical Bean, a brand known for its 100% fairtrade and USDA certified organic coffee, is now widely available in the United States, allowing consumers to trace their coffee's journey from crop to cup using a unique QR code on each bag. The company emphasizes transparency and ethical sourcing, supporting communities in Guatemala through scholarship and aid programs. Ethical Bean offers seven roasts and is available nationwide and online at Walmart and Amazon.

title: Bet on Wild Swings in the Market With the SPXL ETF
summary: The Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X Shares (SPXL) ETF is designed for traders to capitalize on short-term market upswings by delivering three times the gains of the S&P 500, using leverage and investing in fast-rising stocks. While it offers significant profit potential during bullish periods, its leveraged nature and daily resets mean it can also lead to rapid losses during downturns, making it suitable only for active trading rather than buy-and-hold strategies. Investors are cautioned about its high expense ratio and the need for close market monitoring due to its volatility.

title: Walmart rolls out same-day delivery service
summary: Walmart Inc. has launched its Walmart+ subscription membership program, offering free same-day deliveries on groceries and general merchandise for $98 per year or $12.95 per month. The program leverages Walmart's extensive store network to provide services similar to Amazon Prime but at a lower price, aiming to defend its grocery market share rather than directly compete with Amazon. The new service complements Walmart's existing curbside pickup, next-day, and two-day delivery options.

title: Groupon Business Model
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Groupon business model, detailing its history, how it operates as a middleman between merchants and consumers, and how it generates revenue through commissions. It examines Groupon's multi-sided platform, its value propositions for both customer segments, and outlines its key resources, activities, partners, and cost structure. The article also includes a SWOT analysis and identifies competitors, concluding that Groupon still has opportunities for growth despite recent market share loss.

title: Why American Express is trying technology that makes deepfake videos look real
summary: American Express is leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs), the technology behind deepfake videos, to create synthetic financial data for fraud detection. By training these GANs on internal financial data, Amex aims to generate realistic fake credit card transactions to improve machine-learning algorithms in spotting scams more quickly. This approach helps in enhancing cybersecurity systems and protecting customers from financial fraud.

title: Kratos Debuts Their New Wideband Software Receiver — OpenSpace™
summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. has introduced its OpenSpace™ Wideband Software Receiver designed for high data rate Earth Observation (EO) and Remote Sensing missions. This virtual receiver runs on standard x86 servers, offering 600 Mbps throughput and supporting hundreds of MHz of instantaneous bandwidth, mirroring the performance of hardware-based systems but with greater flexibility and cost-effectiveness. It integrates into existing ground architectures and leverages virtualization to reduce reliance on proprietary hardware.

title: Marvell exits the general purpose Arm server business
summary: Marvell Technology Group has announced it is discontinuing its ThunderX3 Arm-based server processor for general-purpose server use. The company will instead focus on vertical markets and hyperscalers, customizing silicon for major cloud providers. This move allows Marvell to secure up-front commitments and reduce risk by co-funding custom chip development with customers.

title: 10 Most Visited Websites by Internet Users in India
summary: This article identifies the top 10 most visited websites in India based on unique visitor data from July 2020. Google Sites, encompassing YouTube, Gmail, and Google Search, leads the list with over 396.9 million unique visitors and a 97.8% reach among Indian internet users. Facebook and Amazon Sites follow, securing the second and third positions respectively.

title: Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien vs. Netgear Orbi 6: Which Wi-Fi 6 router should you buy?
summary: This article compares the Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien and Netgear Orbi WiFi 6 mesh router systems, highlighting their respective strengths and weaknesses. The AmpliFi Alien offers faster wireless speeds, greater coverage, and additional features like AmpliFi Teleport, while the Netgear Orbi 6 distinguishes itself with a 2.5Gbps WAN port and more Ethernet ports, making it suitable for multi-gig wired networks. Ultimately, the AmpliFi Alien is recommended for most users due to its balance of features, speed, and massive coverage for its price point.

title: Which coding languages are used by the world’s top companies?
summary: This article examines the most popular and highest-paying coding languages used by major companies, highlighting an infographic from Flyaps that details the languages adopted by 25 Fortune 500 companies. It discusses how choices in programming languages depend on factors like speed, reliability, and scalability, and contrasts findings from other studies on popular and high-paying languages. Examples of specific companies and the languages they use are also provided.

title: Amazon, Verizon may invest over $4 billion in Vodafone Idea: Report
summary: Amazon and Verizon are reportedly considering investing over $4 billion in India's struggling telecom firm Vodafone Idea. This potential investment comes after a Supreme Court ruling granted mobile carriers 10 years to settle government dues, creating more certainty for Vodafone Idea's survival. The news caused a significant surge in Vodafone Idea's share price.

title: Amazon opens sort center in Erlanger, creating 1,000-plus jobs
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has opened a new sort center in Erlanger, Kentucky, creating over 1,000 new jobs in the region. The company is also implementing measures to ensure employee safety. This expansion is part of Amazon's ongoing growth, as highlighted by related articles detailing their ventures into supermarkets and increased local hiring.

title: Oatly is defending itself after selling stake to Trump donor Schwarzman's Blackstone Group
summary: Oatly, the vegan milk brand, is facing backlash and potential boycotts from its customers and the coffee industry after selling a 10% stake to a group of investors led by Blackstone Growth. The controversy stems from Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman's significant donations to Donald Trump's reelection campaign, and past accusations against Blackstone-owned Hidrovias regarding Amazon deforestation. Oatly is defending its decision, stating the partnership helps expand its sustainable mission and influences leading private equity to invest in sustainability.

title: Mastercard partners with Global Payments’ TSYS to expand installment offerings
summary: Mastercard has partnered with TSYS, a Global Payments company, to offer consumers more flexible payment options by enabling them to split transactions into installments before, during, or after checkout. This collaboration aims to meet the growing demand for flexible payment solutions amidst economic uncertainties, enhancing Mastercard's buy-now-pay-later ecosystem and benefiting issuers and merchants. The partnership focuses on increasing consumer choice, control, and simplicity at checkout, ultimately aiming to boost consumer acquisition, loyalty, and approval rates while decreasing cart abandonment.

title: PVH Corp. Reports 2020 Second Quarter Results and Provides Business Update Relating to COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: PVH Corp. reported second-quarter 2020 results that exceeded expectations despite a 33% revenue decrease to $1.581 billion, driven by strong digital channel growth of over 50%. The company strengthened its financial position with over $2.7 billion in liquidity and is implementing strategic priorities like streamlining North America operations and focusing on digital business to accelerate recovery amidst the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. While anticipating continued negative impact in the second half, PVH expects revenue to decline approximately 25% for that period, but cannot provide more detailed guidance due to pandemic uncertainty.

title: Samsung QLED 4K TV deal takes $100 off the price for Labor Day at Best Buy
summary: Best Buy is offering discounts on Samsung's QLED 4K TVs for Labor Day, with savings up to $500 on larger models. For instance, the 58-inch Q60T Series 4K UHD TV is $100 off, priced at $799.99, and the 85-inch model sees a $500 reduction. The article highlights these deals as an opportunity to purchase a QLED 4K TV at a reduced price before major sales like Amazon Prime Day and Black Friday.

title: Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund Review: Should You Invest?
summary: This article reviews the Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund, which invests in Schroder International Selection Fund Global Equity Alpha. The author discusses the underlying fund's performance against its benchmark, highlighting a poor track record and high expense ratios, especially for the regular plan. The article concludes by recommending investors consider alternatives with lower expenses, such as the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund, for international diversification.

title: Fossil Gen 5 Garrett HR review: Style and substance
summary: The Fossil Gen 5 Garrett HR smartwatch blends classic chronograph style with modern features like hands-free calls, activity tracking, and contactless payments. Its improved hardware provides a smooth user experience, addressing previous Wear OS sluggishness. While battery life is typical for smartwatches, and Google Fit has some limitations, the Garrett HR is praised for its design, vibrant display, and multi-functional capabilities, making it a strong lifestyle-focused smartwatch.

title: Oracle on Google Cloud: Two Deployment Options
summary: This article discusses two primary deployment options for running Oracle on Google Cloud: using partner-managed Oracle instances available on the Google Cloud Marketplace, and setting up a custom Oracle instance via Google's Bare Metal Solution. It outlines the pros and cons of each method, noting that Google Cloud Platform does not directly support running Oracle in a virtual instance due to licensing limitations. NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP is also presented as a solution for enterprise-level Oracle deployments on GCP.

title: Spotify appears to be building a karaoke feature – just as Twitch shuts down Sings
summary: Spotify is reportedly developing an in-app karaoke feature, a move that comes as Amazon-owned Twitch announces the closure of its own karaoke app, Twitch Sings, in January. The new Spotify feature was discovered by reverse engineer Jane Manchun Wong and appears to allow vocal level adjustments. This development aligns with the success seen by other karaoke apps like Tencent Music Entertainment's WeSing, suggesting a growing market for in-app karaoke experiences.

title: District Court Applies Absolute Intervening Rights to Method Claims
summary: A District Court ruled that absolute intervening rights can apply to method claims, siding with Amazon against Vocalife LLC. This decision clarifies that the nature of the infringing activity, rather than the claim type (apparatus or method), determines the applicability of intervening rights under 35 U.S.C. § 252. The court also held that specific products protected by intervening rights could be identified by their date of manufacture, providing crucial guidance for patent practitioners.

title: Slideshow: Amazon's new projects in the works in Central Florida
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is actively developing approximately six new projects across Central Florida, collectively spanning millions of square feet. These developments signify the e-commerce giant's continued expansion in the region. The article highlights the significant scale of these upcoming facilities.

title: Helium Is Soaring on Red-Hot Demand, Shrinking Supply
summary: This article discusses the increasing demand and shrinking supply of helium, highlighting its critical role in various high-tech applications beyond balloons. It points out that new large helium deposits are becoming rare and existing reserves, like the U.S. National Helium Reserve, are projected to be depleted soon. The piece also suggests investment opportunities in helium exploration companies like Desert Mountain Energy, comparing the commodity's rarity to gold.

title: The ABCs of AI
summary: This article provides a primer on artificial intelligence (AI) and its applications, particularly within the printing industry. It explains what AI is, its historical context, and how it can help print businesses optimize operations, cut costs, and streamline workflows, especially in the context of increasing automation and customization demands accelerated by COVID-19. Kodak's PRINERGY Software and On Demand Platform are highlighted as examples of AI-powered solutions in print.

title: Bezos-backed cancer testing company to go public, promises to detect 50+ types from blood draw
summary: Grail Inc., a cancer testing startup funded by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, has filed for an initial public offering in the U.S. The company has developed a multi-cancer early detection blood test designed to identify over 50 types of cancer across all stages, targeting individuals over 50 without symptoms for a planned 2021 launch. While Grail believes its test can significantly increase early cancer diagnoses, some medical experts, like Dr. Ronald Adler, express skepticism about the universal efficacy of early detection for most cancers.

title: AWS Kubernetes Cluster: Quick Setup with EC2 and EKS
summary: This article provides a quick guide to setting up Kubernetes clusters on AWS, focusing on two main deployment options: directly on EC2 instances and using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). It includes step-by-step tutorials for both methods, covering installation, scaling, and configuration. The post also highlights how NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP can be used to provision persistent storage for Kubernetes clusters on AWS.

title: ‘Out of favor’ assets offer opportunity to make big money, says billionaire investor Howard Marks
summary: Billionaire investor Howard Marks suggests that "out of favor" assets like retail and office real estate, and entertainment/hospitality stocks, offer significant return opportunities in a low interest rate environment. While yields on U.S. Treasurys are near zero, making other asset classes seem attractive, their returns may still be lackluster. Marks also advises investors to look beyond short-term market fluctuations, especially concerning recent tech stock sell-offs, and focus on long-term holdings of quality companies.

title: UNILEVER TO ACQUIRE NUTRITION AND WELLNESS BRAND LIQUID I.V.
summary: Unilever has announced its agreement to acquire Liquid I.V., a US-based health-science nutrition and wellness company founded by Brandin Cohen in 2012. Liquid I.V. is known for its electrolyte drink utilizing Cellular Transport Technology (CTT) and has a product range including Hydration, Energy, and Sleep solutions. The acquisition aims to further Unilever's presence in the fast-growing health and wellness sector, with Liquid I.V. continuing to operate from El Segundo, California, under Cohen's leadership.

title: Cancer-detection company Grail, which counts Jeff Bezos among its investors, files to go public
summary: Grail, a biotechnology company focused on developing a blood test for early-stage cancer detection, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO). The company, which counts Jeff Bezos and Illumina among its investors, currently has no product or revenue and reported a significant loss in the first half of 2020. Grail aims to use the IPO funds to finance extensive clinical trials and prove the safety and efficacy of its "Galleri" test.

title: Amazon’s Beaumont fulfillment center is now open for business
summary: Amazon's new fulfillment center in Beaumont, California, is now open, employing over 1,000 full-time associates. The facility will be used to pick, pack, and ship small items, and Amazon emphasizes its competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, and commitment to the Beaumont community. The company has also detailed its extensive COVID-19 safety measures and its significant investments and job creation in California.

title: Amazon, Ford loom large on Livonia's 2019 tax rolls
summary: Livonia's top taxpayers in 2019 included major corporations like Amazon and Ford, significantly contributing to the city's budget alongside other large businesses such as Consumers Energy and DTE Energy. The city prioritizes working with businesses to ensure tax payments and retention, often granting tax exemptions under Michigan's Act 198 to companies that maintain employment levels and benefit the city. While Livonia City Council has final say on these exemptions, the overall goal is to keep businesses thriving within the community.

title: Ex-NSA chief Keith Alexander joins Amazon board
summary: Former National Security Agency chief Keith Alexander has joined the board of Amazon.com Inc as of September 9, 2020. Alexander, who also serves as co-chief executive officer of IronNet Cybersecurity Inc, will be part of Amazon's four-member audit committee. He previously commanded the U.S. Cyber Command and headed the Central Security Service.

title: AWS Big Data: 6 Options You Should Consider
summary: This article explores six key AWS big data analytics options: Amazon Kinesis, EMR, Glue, Machine Learning, Redshift, and QuickSight. It details how AWS solutions manage the entire big data lifecycle from collection to consumption and visualization. The piece also highlights how NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP integrates with AWS to enhance database workloads and provide robust storage management for big data deployments.

title: Ambani’s Reliance to Offer $20 Billion Stake in Retail Arm to Amazon
summary: Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries Ltd. is reportedly offering a $20 billion stake in its retail business, Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd., to Amazon. Amazon has engaged in discussions and expressed interest in a potential transaction, with Reliance willing to sell up to a 40% stake in the subsidiary.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Raised Prices on Essentials Amid Pandemic, Watchdog Says
summary: A consumer watchdog group, Public Citizen, released a report accusing Amazon of price gouging on essential items like hand sanitizer and disposable gloves during the COVID-19 pandemic. The report claims price increases of up to 1,000% compared to pre-pandemic levels or other retailers. Amazon, in response, has called for a federal price-gouging law.

title: -Oracle wins cloud business from McDonald's, Albertson's
summary: Oracle Corp announced significant new deals to provide cloud computing services to McDonald's Corp, Albertsons Companies Inc, Humana Inc, and business software firm Xactly. These wins indicate Oracle's effort to compete with larger cloud providers like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure by expanding its customer base and infrastructure. Xactly, in particular, will be moving the majority of its computing work to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure from its own co-located data centers.

title: Four Nashvillians made Forbes' annual list of the 400 richest people in America
summary: Four residents of Nashville, including Tommy Frist Jr. and Martha Ingram, were named to Forbes' annual list of the 400 richest people in America. This article highlights their inclusion in the prestigious ranking, with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos topping the national list. It also references previous Forbes mentions related to Nashville's billionaires and most valuable companies.

title: Our Ecosystem of Technology Partners for Federal Agencies
summary: ICF highlights its extensive ecosystem of technology partners dedicated to accelerating modernization efforts and integrating cutting-edge capabilities for federal agencies. These strategic partnerships enable ICF to deliver tailored, scalable solutions that enhance operational efficiency, ensure secure transformation, and drive measurable impact, particularly in areas like AI advancement. The article underscores how these partnerships facilitate high-impact, interoperable industry solutions that streamline processes and improve service delivery for various sectors including U.S. federal government, health, utilities, and energy markets.

title: Walmart tightens on-time, in-full requirements
summary: Walmart is increasing its on-time, in-full (OTIF) delivery requirements for suppliers and carriers to 98% across all goods, effective September 15, 2020. Non-compliance will result in a 3% fine on the cost of goods. This change aims to improve product availability for customers, especially as e-commerce demand surges during the pandemic and with the rollout of the Walmart+ program.

title: E-commerce surge spurs race for electric delivery vehicles
summary: The surge in e-commerce is driving a competitive race among companies to develop and deploy electric delivery vehicles. This includes Amazon's order of 100,000 electric vans from Rivian, highlighting the growing demand for sustainable logistics solutions. The article touches on related automotive news, specifically detailing new dealer census data, and insights regarding tariffs and their impact on new vehicle prices.

title: FedEx senses need for real-time parcel tracking
summary: FedEx is introducing SenseAware ID, a new sensor-based logistics device for real-time parcel tracking, particularly aimed at critical shipments like eventual COVID-19 vaccine deliveries. This initiative is part of FedEx's broader strategy to enhance its global shipping experience and improve safety and timeliness in response to increasing delivery demands. The technology will initially be rolled out for First Overnight shipments in the U.S. and expanded to more customers in 2021.

title: Macy’s Sees Smaller Stores Both Inside & Outside Of Malls As Road To Survival
summary: Macy's plans to open smaller, non-mall locations and downsize existing stores to adapt to changing retail landscapes and survive the challenges posed by the pandemic. The company aims to move beyond its traditional anchor role in struggling malls, focusing on off-mall and smaller format stores for Macy's and Bloomingdale's while maintaining a presence in thriving high-end malls. This strategy comes as Macy's dodged bankruptcy with $4.5 billion in financing, contrasting with other department stores like J.C. Penney and Neiman Marcus, which filed for Chapter 11.

title: Amazon Air Is Growing Fast During the Pandemic
summary: Amazon Air significantly expanded its operations during the pandemic, adding nine aircraft between May and July, the most in any three-month period for the company. Its fleet grew to 54 planes, with increased daily flight activity and utilization. Researchers predict Amazon's fleet could reach 200 aircraft by 2028 and expect further international and domestic expansion to smaller airports.

title: Amazon to hire 100,000 more workers in its latest job spree this year
summary: Amazon announced it is hiring an additional 100,000 full and part-time workers in the U.S. and Canada, primarily for new warehouse and operations roles. This marks the fourth hiring surge for the company this year, driven by increased e-commerce demand during the pandemic. Despite expanding automation, Amazon continues to require significant human labor to manage its growing online retail operations.

title: How Oracle, now partnering with TikTok, became the Trump administration’s favorite tech company.
summary: The article details how Oracle became the Trump administration's preferred tech company, culminating in its partnership with TikTok over Microsoft. It highlights Oracle's strong ties to Trump through its co-founder Larry Ellison and CEO Safra Catz, who supported his reelection campaign. The article also describes instances where the White House sided with Oracle in legal disputes and controversies, like the Google lawsuit and the JEDI contract, and Oracle's involvement during the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Amazon to hire 3,600 for new jobs in Michigan
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is hiring 3,600 people for new jobs in its warehouses and delivery stations across Michigan, part of a drive to fill 100,000 positions across the United States and Canada. This expansion brings Amazon's total jobs in Michigan to 13,500 and is seen as good news for the state economy, which is recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic. The company offers competitive wages, benefits, and tuition prepayment programs.

title: The Oracle-TikTok Deal Sure Worked Out Well for a Close Trump Ally
summary: Oracle secured a deal to become TikTok's "trusted tech partner" in the U.S., beating out Microsoft, a move that requires White House approval. This agreement is viewed critically due to Oracle's close ties with the Trump administration, including co-founder Larry Ellison hosting a fundraiser and CEO Safra Catz serving on Trump's transition team. The article suggests these connections may have strategically influenced the outcome of the deal amid Trump's earlier threats to ban TikTok.

title: Looking at the future - Mukesh Ambani keeps Carlyle Group and SoftBank waiting as RIL juggernaut picks pace
summary: Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) is experiencing strong investor demand for its retail business, leading to Carlyle Group Inc. and SoftBank Group Corp. being placed on a waiting list. RIL is seeking funding for Reliance Retail by tapping backers of its digital services business, which has already secured $20 billion. The company plans to sell about a 10% stake in Reliance Retail, with a significant allocation reserved for Amazon.com Inc., which could acquire up to a 40% holding.

title: Exclusive: Alibaba, China Mobile weigh $443 mln investment in blacklisted Dahua - sources
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and China Mobile Communications Group Co Ltd are considering a 3 billion yuan ($443 million) investment in Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co Ltd, a Chinese surveillance equipment maker that was blacklisted by the U.S. The investment would involve a private share placement, and China Mobile is also negotiating a significant business agreement with Dahua for its big data and cloud computing services. This move comes as China expands its "smart city" initiatives, driving demand for surveillance technology.

title: Why Amazon Outhustles Comcast: A Tale Of Two Monopolies And Implications For Their Customers
summary: This article compares Amazon and Comcast, labeling them both as monopolies, but highlighting their differing approaches to customer service and innovation. It argues that while Comcast, a government-created "natural monopoly," suffers from complacency due to lack of competition, Amazon thrives by continuously innovating and prioritizing customer satisfaction despite its market dominance. The author suggests that government protection leads to lethargy, whereas market-driven monopolies are forced to remain nimble.

title: CMO Of The Week: Intuit’s Lara Hood Balazs
summary: This article features Lara Hood Balazs, CMO and General Manager – Strategic Partner Group at Intuit, highlighting how her team rapidly adapted marketing strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly after the tax deadline extension. Balazs discusses Intuit's initiatives like the QuickBooks PPP program and their support for the Black and LGBTQ+ communities. She also elaborates on the company's shift from live events to virtual platforms and her philosophy of customer-centric marketing.

title: Walmart launches Amazon Prime subscription competitor, 'Walmart+'
summary: Walmart has launched its new subscription program, "Walmart+", to compete with Amazon Prime. For $12.95 a month or $98 a year, subscribers receive benefits like unlimited free same-day delivery, fuel discounts, and a touch-free in-store shopping experience. This initiative aims to cater to consumer demand for faster online purchase delivery and integrates previous services like "Delivery Unlimited."

title: 10 masks that don't go behind your ears
summary: This article highlights face masks that do not require ear loops, catering to individuals with sensitive ears or those wearing glasses/hearing aids. It provides a list of ten such masks, ranging from tie-on designs to those with head straps, and includes options from various brands and retailers. The article also touches on mask extenders as an alternative for existing ear-loop masks and reiterates CDC recommendations for masking.

title: VyprVPN Review
summary: VyprVPN is a virtual private network service that offers strong privacy commitments, a wide geographic distribution of servers, and the latest VPN technology including WireGuard and its custom Chameleon protocol. While its monthly subscription is pricey compared to competitors, the annual plan is much more affordable. The service lacks some advanced features like multihop connections and split-tunneling but excels in privacy by owning its server infrastructure and having a clear no-log policy, backed by a third-party audit.

title: FedEx Posts Strong Quarterly Earnings, Fueled by E-Commerce
summary: FedEx reported strong fiscal first-quarter earnings, exceeding Wall Street expectations, largely driven by a surge in e-commerce deliveries due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The company plans to hire 70,000 additional employees and implement a 4.9% rate increase in January, while also preparing for increased demand during an unprecedented holiday season and the potential distribution of COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Amazon launches Luxury Stores for selected Amazon Prime members
summary: Amazon has launched "Luxury Stores," a new shopping platform exclusively for selected Amazon Prime members, offering high-end brands. The service, initially featuring Oscar de la Renta, allows brands to control inventory and pricing while Amazon provides merchandising tools. This initiative aims to expand Amazon's reach into the luxury market and offers customers enhanced viewing options for products.

title: Exclusive: -AT&T considers cellphone plans subsidized by ads
authors: ['Sheila Dang', 'Helen Coster', 'Krystal Hu and Kenneth Li']
summary: AT&T is exploring offering wireless phone plans partially subsidized by advertising as early as next year, according to CEO John Stankey. This move aligns with AT&T's commitment to advertising and its efforts to reduce debt by potentially selling assets like its advertising-technology unit Xandr. The company believes that a segment of its customer base would accept ads for a reduction in their mobile bill, leveraging better ad targeting and its upcoming ad-supported HBO Max service.

title: Snowflake Stock: What You Need to Know About Tech’s Hottest IPO
summary: Snowflake Inc., a data-managing firm founded in 2012, has become Silicon Valley's hottest new public company. It helps companies like Capital One and Electronic Arts manage and analyze data stored on cloud services from providers such as Amazon and Microsoft. The company stated in its IPO filing that it is competing in a market valued at over $80 billion.

title: Amazon Plans to Put 1,000 Warehouses in Suburban Neighborhoods
summary: Amazon plans to open 1,000 small delivery hubs in cities and suburbs across the U.S., eventually expanding to about 1,500. This strategy aims to bring products closer to customers for faster delivery, leveraging proximity to compete with brick-and-mortar rivals like Walmart and Target, and decreasing reliance on partners like UPS. The expansion will increase Amazon's self-delivery capabilities but may lead to conflicts with local residents over increased traffic and the industrial nature of these facilities.

title: ZWIFT RAISES $450 MILLION INVESTMENT; SERIES C ROUND LED BY KKR
summary: Zwift, the online fitness platform, announced a $450 million minority investment led by KKR, with additional investors including Permira, Specialized Bicycle Components’ venture capital fund, Zone 5 Ventures, and the Amazon Alexa Fund. The funding will be used to accelerate the development of Zwift’s core software platform and bring Zwift-designed hardware to market, enhancing the user experience. The company plans to expand its global presence in the at-home gamified fitness subscription business and invest in product innovation and headcount.

title: Illumina in talks to buy cancer testing startup Grail - Bloomberg News
summary: Gene sequencing company Illumina Inc is reportedly in late talks to acquire cancer testing startup Grail Inc. The deal could value Grail at over $6 billion, surpasses its previous fundraising valuations, and an announcement could come as early as this week. Illumina, already Grail's largest shareholder with a 14.6% stake, previously founded Grail in 2016.

title: Small Tech Stocks Soar as the Future Arrives Early (Published 2020)
summary: Smaller technology companies specializing in software, streaming, security, and e-commerce are experiencing significant stock market gains, mirroring the performance of tech giants. This surge is attributed to the accelerated adoption of remote work and online services during the coronavirus pandemic. Experts note an unprecedented shift in workforce dynamics, suggesting these trends will continue to drive the growth of these smaller tech firms.

title: Introducing the Forrester Wave for CCaaS 2020
summary: Forrester's latest Wave report for CCaaS in 2020 evaluated 10 key providers based on 33 criteria, identifying leaders, strong performers, and contenders. Five9, Talkdesk, Genesys, and NICE inContact were named leaders, highlighting their strengths in areas like WFO technology, global deployments, and innovative roadmaps. The report serves as a guide for companies considering new purchases in the contact center as a service market.

title: Amazon plans 1,000 small delivery hubs in cities, neighborhoods across U.S.
summary: Amazon.com Inc. plans to open 1,000 small delivery hubs across the U.S. to bring products closer to customers and offer faster delivery, particularly in response to increased online shopping during COVID-19 lockdowns and to compete with Walmart and Target. These hubs, which will eventually number around 1,500, are part of Amazon's strategy to reduce reliance on partners like UPS and the U.S. Postal Service by building its own logistics network closer to residential areas. The expansion presents challenges for urban planning and concerns from local residents regarding increased traffic and the visual impact of warehouses in their neighborhoods.

title: Epic is not EXACTly the Microsoft of Madison
summary: This article argues that while Epic Systems Corp. is often compared to Microsoft in terms of its regional economic impact, the comparison is flawed. The author, through Erik Iverson of WARF, suggests that Exact Sciences, due to its publicly traded nature and broad employee stock options, is more akin to Madison's Microsoft, creating localized wealth. The article also details Epic's private stock plan for employees, noting its differences from Microsoft's early model.

title: 10 monopolies and why they make good investments
summary: This article explores the investment potential of monopolies and oligopolies, guided by insights from Peter Thiel and Warren Buffett on competitive advantage. It identifies ten companies with strong monopolistic or oligopolistic market positions, such as Amazon, Google, Facebook, Visa, and Airbus, highlighting their market shares and business models. The author also discusses the transient nature of monopolies, using examples like Kodak and Nokia, and suggests investing in a "moat" ETF for diversified exposure to such companies.

title: IBM Remains America’s Worst Big Tech Company
summary: Despite a change in CEO, IBM continues to underperform significantly compared to other major tech companies, with its stock price declining while competitors surge. The company has experienced nearly six years of revenue decline and its cloud operations show minimal growth, placing it outside the top 50 American companies by market capitalization. IBM lacks strong consumer-focused products and its key brands like Watson and The Weather Channel fail to provide compelling growth engines, indicating a dim future for its return to the top tier of tech.

title: Jakks Pacific Unveils ‘Treats at Home: Halloween’ with Super Mario, Frozen II Characters
summary: Jakks Pacific is launching a new product range called "Treats at Home: Halloween" featuring Super Mario and Frozen II characters, designed to facilitate virtual trick-or-treating experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. These sets include figures and accessories, along with postcard invitations for families to host virtual Halloween events via video conferencing. The initiative aims to blend seasonal celebration with product engagement and costume promotion.

title: Coatesville Resident Once Again Makes Forbes 400 List of Wealthiest Americans
summary: Campbell Soup heiress Mary Alice Dorrance Malone, a Coatesville resident, has once again been named to The Forbes 400 list of wealthiest Americans, coming in at No. 213 with a net worth of $3.7 billion. Her wealth makes her the third-richest person in Pennsylvania. Dorrance Malone is the largest shareholder of the Campbell Soup Company and president of Iron Spring Farm.

title: ESG sees record inflows amid pandemic. One leading issuer on the theme's staying power
summary: ESG investing has seen record inflows in 2020, with over $19 billion flowing into ESG ETFs, bringing the total to over $40 billion. Luke Oliver of DWS Group attributes this growth to investors adopting ESG as a core portfolio strategy, noting that ESG companies are often better prepared for future challenges. The trend is fueled by increased awareness of environmental and social issues, along with a shift away from sectors like fossil fuels.

title: TikTok Ban Averted: Trump Gives Oracle-Walmart Deal His 'Blessing'
summary: President Trump has tentatively approved a deal involving Oracle and Walmart to keep TikTok operational in the U.S., averting a ban set for midnight, Sunday. The agreement aims to address national security concerns regarding American user data, even though Chinese company ByteDance is expected to retain a majority ownership stake. This deal is expected to boost Oracle's cloud computing business and allow Walmart to integrate e-commerce into the app.

title: -Illumina to buy Jeff Bezos-backed cancer testing firm Grail in $8 bln deal
summary: Illumina announced its plan to acquire Grail Inc., a cancer screening startup backed by investors including Jeff Bezos, in an $8 billion cash-and-stock deal. Grail is developing a liquid biopsy test for early cancer detection, a field Illumina's CEO sees as critical for genomics in the coming decade. Despite the strategic fit, Illumina's shares fell following the announcement, with some analysts questioning the timing of acquiring a company still in critical clinical development stages.

title: The enduring fan base that boosts Bath & Body Works
summary: Bath & Body Works has cultivated a deeply loyal customer base, which has been a key factor in its consistent success, even during the pandemic. Unlike its struggling sister brand, Victoria's Secret, Bath & Body Works has thrived by engaging enthusiasts who collect and discuss its products, leveraging seasonal releases and varied packaging to create a "gamified" shopping experience. The retailer's focus on affordable luxury and essential home and personal care items proved particularly relevant during the pandemic, further boosting its sales and ensuring its strong market position.

title: Illumina to buy Jeff Bezos-backed cancer testing firm Grail in $8 billion deal
summary: Illumina announced its plan to acquire Grail Inc., a cancer screening startup it originally spun off, in an $8 billion cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition will give Illumina access to Grail's "liquid biopsy" blood test, Galleri, expected to launch in 2021. Despite criticism from analysts regarding the fit and potential conflicts with existing customers, Illumina aims to capitalize on the rapidly growing market for liquid biopsies, estimated to be worth tens of billions of dollars.

title: Walmart aims to capture market share with new private-label clothing line
summary: Walmart is launching a new private-label clothing brand called "Free Assembly" to attract budget-conscious consumers who are moving away from traditional mall-based department stores. The line offers modern styling at affordable prices, ranging from $9 to $45, and will be available in 250 stores and online. This initiative is part of Walmart's broader strategy to expand its presence in the clothing market, despite past mixed results with fashion acquisitions.

title: Illumina will pay $8B to acquire Grail, the Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos-backed cancer detection company
summary: Illumina has announced its acquisition of Grail, a cancer detection startup backed by Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos, for $8 billion in cash and stock. Grail, which was spun out of Illumina, had been preparing for an IPO and plans to launch a multi-cancer early detection test in 2021. The news led to an over 8% drop in Illumina's shares on Monday.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Investing In Battery Recycling Company Redwood Materials
summary: Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) is investing in Redwood Materials, a battery recycling startup founded by former Tesla executive JB Straubel, as part of Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund. The investment aims to enhance sustainability by recycling batteries from Amazon's diverse operations, including Amazon Web Services, consumer electronics, and its growing electric logistics fleet. Redwood Materials will specifically focus on recycling batteries for electric vehicles and lithium-ion batteries.

title: Kroger steps up AI deployment to combat checkout losses
summary: Kroger has partnered with the Irish AI firm Everseen to install computer vision technology at up to 2,500 self-checkout stations. This system detects unscanned items and alerts employees to combat retail shrink, which cost retailers $61.7 billion in losses in 2019. The deployment is part of a broader industry trend to leverage AI and advanced cameras to reduce theft and automate checkout processes, especially relevant during the pandemic for minimizing contact.

title: Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien router review: An essential Wi-Fi 6 work-from-home upgrade
summary: The Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien router delivers excellent whole-home Wi-Fi 6 coverage and is easy to set up and manage, making it a great upgrade for homes looking to switch to Wi-Fi 6 given its performance and unique features like Teleport. While it has some drawbacks like the lack of a 160MHz channel and dedicated mesh backhaul, it offers significant performance gains over Wi-Fi 5 options. Its distinctive design with a large LCD screen makes real-time network monitoring user-friendly.

title: Oracle is a distant laggard in cloud infrastructure market even after TikTok deal
summary: Despite recent high-profile customer wins like TikTok and Zoom, Oracle remains a "niche player" in the cloud infrastructure market, significantly trailing leaders Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Gartner estimates Oracle's market share at around 2%, and analysts note that its growth is still heavily reliant on traditional database software, with its stock performance lagging behind major cloud competitors. The TikTok deal, while a "shot in the arm," is viewed by some analysts as politically motivated rather than a testament to Oracle's competitive cloud capabilities.

title: One of the world’s biggest cabinet firms plans facility in southern Dallas
summary: American Woodmark Corp., one of the world's largest cabinet manufacturers, is planning to open a new 298,000 square foot distribution facility in southern Dallas. This will be an addition to their existing three facilities in North Texas, capitalizing on the region's strong homebuilding market. The facility will be located in Trammell Crow Co.'s Altamoore Drive business park.

title: FedEx Ground will hire 300 for distribution center in Kansas City's Northland Park
summary: FedEx Ground is opening a new 548,500-square-foot large package distribution center in Northland Park, Kansas City, in October. The company plans to hire 300 employees for the facility. This marks FedEx Ground's lease of the largest industrial building in Northland Park, developed by NorthPoint Development.

title: AgEagle Aerial Systems: Termination Of Ridiculous Amazon E-Commerce Pipedream Should Send Stock Back To Penny Territory (NYSE:UAVS)
summary: This article argues that AgEagle Aerial Systems (UAVS) stock is significantly overvalued due to speculation about an Amazon e-commerce delivery drone partnership. The author details AgEagle's historically small operations, low revenues, limited employees, and unsophisticated facilities, suggesting that the company's fundamentals do not support its high share price. The piece concludes that the stock should return to penny territory once the "pipedream" of an Amazon partnership is dispelled.

title: Who Owns Etsy and Will It Eventually Sell Out?
summary: Etsy is an e-commerce marketplace for unique goods, owned by Etsy Inc. since its founding in 2005. Despite common business practices of selling out, Etsy has maintained its independence and acquired other companies instead. While headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, it also has a subsidiary office in Dublin, Ireland, which helps reduce its tax obligations.

title: Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF (QYLG), including its current price, performance metrics, expenses, and holdings. It also contrasts QYLG with other ETFs in similar categories based on factors like expense ratio, assets under management, and year-to-date returns. The report offers an in-depth analysis of the ETF's concentration, valuation, dividend, fund flows, and ESG scores, giving a comprehensive overview for potential investors.

title: Stacy's Rise Project Expands Commitment to Female Founders; Partners with Hello Alice to Fund $150,000 in Grants to Black Women Business Owners
summary: The Stacy's Rise Project, in partnership with Hello Alice, is expanding its program to support an additional 15 Black female founders with $150,000 in business grants, professional advertising, and executive coaching. This initiative addresses the significant disparity in venture capitalist funding for women of color and aims to help these entrepreneurs overcome unique challenges identified in a recent survey. The program will also include a complimentary membership in The BOSS Network and will promote the businesses of the selected founders.

title: Amazon’s ‘Climate Pledge Friendly’ to Make It Easier for Customers to Discover, Shop for Sustainable Products
summary: Amazon has launched "Climate Pledge Friendly," a new program designed to help customers easily find and shop for sustainable products. The initiative features over 25,000 products endorsed by 19 trusted third-party sustainability certifiers and introduces "Compact by Design," an Amazon-developed certification aimed at reducing carbon emissions through more efficient product design. This program aligns with Amazon's broader commitment to reach net-zero carbon by 2040, ten years ahead of the Paris Agreement.

title: Nasdaq 100 Is Just Halfway Through Its Plunge, Says Morgan Stanley
summary: Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist, Michael Wilson, believes the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 is only halfway through its market correction despite a recent bounce. He points to continued overvaluation, strong call option interest, successful tech IPOs, and hedge fund commitment as signs that bullish sentiment for major tech companies like FAANGs and Microsoft remains too high, indicating further declines are likely. The Nasdaq 100 has already seen a significant drop this month, underperforming the S&P 500.

title: Amazon buys Pentagon City hotel, now has full control over superblock as vision for HQ2 expands
summary: Amazon has purchased the Pentagon City Residence Inn by Marriott, giving it complete control over the superblock designated for its HQ2 expansion. This acquisition is a strategic move to facilitate the second phase of HQ2, with plans to demolish the hotel. This further solidifies Amazon's vision for growth in the Pentagon City area.

title: KKR to invest $755 mln in retail arm of India's Reliance
summary: Private equity firm KKR & Co Inc will invest $755 million in Reliance Industries Ltd's retail unit, bringing its total funding in Reliance Retail to $1.78 billion within a month. This investment, which gives KKR a 1.28% stake, values Reliance Retail at 4.21 trillion rupees ($57 billion). The move aims to strengthen Reliance Retail's financial position as it competes with major e-commerce players like Amazon and Walmart in India.

title: UnitedHealth in Talks to Buy Pharmacy Startup DivvyDose
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. is reportedly in advanced discussions to acquire DivvyDose, an online pharmacy startup, for approximately $300 million. This potential acquisition highlights the ongoing consolidation and competition in the online pharmacy sector, following Amazon's purchase of PillPack in 2018.

title: Is the VGS ETF the best for passive investing?
summary: This article examines the Vanguard MSCI Index International Shares ETF (ASX: VGS) as a strong option for passive investing due to its broad diversification across over 1,500 businesses in major developed countries. It highlights VGS's sector allocation, top holdings including tech giants, and its average annual return of 9.65% over the past five years. The piece concludes that while VGS offers good diversification, investors should consider its management fee compared to other ETFs and explore various options for growth and dividends.

title: Honest Company Founder Jessica Alba: Ethics shouldn’t be a ‘marketing ploy’
summary: Jessica Alba, founder of The Honest Company, states that ethics should be an inherent part of a company's model rather than just a marketing ploy, and that businesses can achieve both social good and profitability. She highlights how The Honest Company's commitment to ethical practices and transparency gives it a competitive advantage, despite past challenges. The company has seen significant growth, partly due to new disinfectant products during the pandemic, and aims to continue positively influencing how other companies operate.

title: We tested Sysco@Home’s new restaurant-quality food delivery service
summary: This article reviews Sysco@Home, a new food delivery service from Sysco Canada that provides restaurant-quality ingredients to consumers. The author tested the service, praising its easy ordering process, bulk options, and the high quality of the food received, such as striploin steaks and mini vegan chocolate cakes. Sysco@Home is highlighted as an ideal option for larger families or those seeking to prepare restaurant-worthy meals at home, especially with upcoming holidays.

title: JBG Smith looks to upgrade a Crystal City park with new retail and a 'water bar'
summary: JBG Smith is planning to upgrade a park in Crystal City, incorporating new retail spaces and a unique "water bar." This development comes amidst other activities by Amazon in the area and JBG Smith's previous warnings about potential COVID-19 impacts on development. Additionally, New York City's Tacombi tacos is expected to open across the street.

title: The coronavirus economy’s 7 biggest winners and losers
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the global economy, creating major winners and losers. Companies like Zoom, Amazon, big-box retailers, Clorox, Peloton, video game companies, and Top Glove saw massive growth due to shifts in consumer behavior and demand for their products. Conversely, airlines, clothing stores, restaurants, ride-hailing services, movie theaters, hotels, casinos, and to a lesser extent, Google, suffered substantial losses and operational challenges.

title: To Fight Apple and Google, Smaller App Rivals Organize a Coalition (Published 2020)
summary: Smaller app developers like Spotify, Match Group, and Epic Games have formed the "Coalition for App Fairness" to challenge the dominance and app store practices of Apple and Google. This move comes as scrutiny intensifies on major tech companies for alleged antitrust violations. The coalition aims to advocate for changes in app store policies and "protect the app economy."

title: U.S. retailer Ulta Beauty shelves plans for Canadian expansion
summary: U.S. cosmetics retailer Ulta Beauty Inc. has cancelled its plans for expansion into Canada, citing the current operating environment and a desire to prioritize growth in its U.S. operations. The decision will cost the company US$55-million to US$65-million this fiscal year. This move comes as the company faced significant financial setbacks during the novel coronavirus pandemic, with comparable-store sales falling and net income plummeting.

title: 3 quick reasons I like the IOO ETF
summary: The iShares Global 100 ETF (ASX: IOO) is recommended for its three key features: diversification from the Australian market, exposure to global developed and emerging markets, and investment in strong, growing businesses with entrenched economic moats. The article highlights its holdings in major global companies like Apple and Microsoft, and its 10-year average annual return of 13.1%. The author suggests it's a good option for investors seeking to diversify beyond ASX shares.

title: Amazon Handmade celebrates five years of its U.S. store and gives back to Makers
summary: Amazon Handmade is celebrating five years since its U.S. launch, having significantly expanded its global selection and active Makers base. The platform has enabled many Makers to achieve over $1 million in annual sales, supporting entrepreneurs worldwide. To mark the anniversary, Amazon Handmade awarded five U.S. Makers $15,000 each after a customer voting process, aiming to help them further grow their businesses.

title: Amazon’s Fleet of Used Airplanes Makes Green Pledge Harder to Keep
summary: Amazon's reliance on older, converted Boeing 767s for its rapidly expanding cargo fleet makes it challenging to meet its ambitious climate pledges despite growing e-commerce demand. These used aircraft are more fuel-guzzling than newer models, leading to higher emissions, even though they offer significant cost savings compared to acquiring new planes. This economic advantage creates a tension between profitability and environmental sustainability for Amazon and other cargo carriers as they grapple with increasing freight volumes.

title: Photos: Men's Wearhouse introduces first 'next gen' store near The Woodlands
summary: Men's Wearhouse has opened its first "next gen" store near The Woodlands, Houston, undergoing a major facelift. This development comes as brick-and-mortar retailers, especially those specializing in formal wear, face significant challenges due to the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact on office work and social events. The article includes photos of the redesigned store.

title: Harte Hanks Hires Digital Agency Veteran and Entrepreneur Drew Rayman To Lead New DTC & eCommerce Offering
summary: Harte Hanks, a customer experience company, announced the appointment of Drew Rayman as Managing Director, eCommerce. Rayman will be responsible for launching and overseeing a new Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) and eCommerce offering, which includes branding, data strategy, marketing, fulfillment, and customer service for businesses. This move aims to enhance Harte Hanks' capabilities in customer-centric commerce, leveraging Rayman's extensive experience in digital agencies and entrepreneurship.

title: Amazon’s Drone Delivery Fleet Hits Milestone With FAA Clearance
summary: Amazon Prime Air has received certification from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to operate as a drone airline, allowing it to begin commercial deliveries under a trial program in the U.S. This makes Amazon one of only a few companies, alongside Wing and UPS, to achieve this crucial step towards widespread drone delivery. While this is a significant milestone, routine deliveries are still years away as regulatory and technical hurdles, such as autonomous flight standards and low-altitude air traffic systems, still need to be addressed.

title: Amazon launches "Climate Pledge Friendly" program
summary: Amazon is launching "Climate Pledge Friendly," a new program labeling over 25,000 products with sustainability certifications, making it easier for customers to find eco-friendly options. The initiative includes a new certification called "Compact by Design" which focuses on product efficiency to reduce carbon emissions through better packaging and design. This program supports Amazon's commitment to be net-zero carbon by 2040 and aligns with the Paris Agreement.

title: Worried about more shortages, grocery stores are stockpiling goods
summary: Grocery stores across the U.S. are stockpiling products like paper towels, Clorox wipes, and even holiday turkeys and cold remedies to avoid shortages during a potential second wave of coronavirus. This strategy shifts from stocking weeks to months worth of supplies, driven by consumer hoarding and ongoing demand, which has also led to higher prices. Manufacturers like Clorox anticipate shortages well into 2021 despite increased production efforts.

title: UnitedHealth has acquired DivvyDose, a competitor to Amazon's PillPack
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired DivvyDose, a start-up that competes with Amazon's PillPack by delivering pre-sorted medications to patients, especially those with chronic conditions. The deal was reportedly valued at just over $300 million. This acquisition reflects a larger trend of retailers and health plans investing in online pharmacy services to broaden their customer base and footprint in the pharmacy market.

title: American Express, Amazon Roll Out UK Credit Card Aimed At SMBs
summary: American Express and Amazon have launched a co-branded credit card in the U.K. aimed at small to medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Named the Amazon Business American Express Card and the Amazon Business Prime American Express Card, these offerings provide rewards and payment flexibility to help businesses manage cash flow. This initiative comes as a significant percentage of British SMBs face cash flow issues, leading them to delay necessary purchases.

title: Good story, bad investment
summary: Thematic ETFs often present compelling narratives around long-term trends like AI or electric vehicles, but Morningstar analyst Alex Bryan warns that a good story doesn't guarantee a sound investment. Investors must successfully bet on three factors: the macro trend playing out, the portfolio companies significantly benefiting, and the market not having already priced in the growth. Historically, most thematic ETFs underperform and many fail to survive long-term, making caution and thorough due diligence essential.

title: Amazon HQ2 just got a lot bigger with the purchase of 1.5 acres in Pentagon City
summary: Amazon has expanded its HQ2 footprint with the acquisition of 1.5 acres in Pentagon City for $148.5 million. This purchase brings Amazon's total control in the area to an 11.6-acre superblock, with plans to submit a vision for the PenPlace site in 2021.

title: Walmart to redesign nearly 1,000 stores
summary: Walmart plans to redesign nearly 1,000 stores with an airport-inspired, digitally-enabled look that incorporates the Walmart app, self-checkout, and contactless payments. The overhaul will begin this fiscal year with 200 locations and expand to almost 1,000 stores by the next fiscal year. This initiative aims to enhance the customer experience and integrate digital and in-store shopping.

title: Walmart brings online shopping experience in stores with app-driven redesign
summary: Walmart is redesigning its Supercenters to integrate the online shopping experience into its physical stores, aiming to encourage app usage and streamline customer navigation. The redesign, inspired by airport wayfinding systems, will include updated signage, self-checkout kiosks, and contactless payment options. This initiative follows a trend among other retailers like Amazon and Whole Foods to merge in-store and online shopping experiences.

title: UnitedHealth Group buys DivvyDose to compete with Amazon's PillPack: report
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired DivvyDose, an online pharmacy startup, for over $300 million to enter the online pharmacy market and compete with Amazon's PillPack. DivvyDose specializes in delivering pre-sorted medications to patients with multiple chronic conditions. This acquisition highlights a growing trend of health plans and retailers investing in digital pharmacy solutions to serve the increasing number of consumers managing chronic illnesses.

title: Amazon confirms plans for 1,000-job west Charlotte facility
summary: Amazon has confirmed plans to open a new facility in west Charlotte, creating over 1,000 full- and part-time jobs. This announcement comes as the e-commerce giant expands its presence in the Charlotte area, with the new facility located at WestPark 85. The company previously stated it would hire 1,100 full- and part-time staff across two new local facilities.

title: AmEx and Amazon Business launch credit card for SMBs
summary: American Express (AmEx) and Amazon Business have introduced new credit cards specifically for small-medium businesses (SMBs) to help them manage finances, especially during economic challenges like COVID-19. The cards offer benefits such as Amazon Rewards points, flexible payment terms, and spending insights, with a Prime version providing enhanced rewards for Amazon Business Prime customers. This partnership aims to provide SMBs with easier access to goods and improved financial tools, leveraging the strengths of both companies.

title: American Express and Amazon launch credit cards for small businesses
summary: American Express and Amazon Business have partnered to launch two new co-branded credit cards for small businesses in the UK: the Business American Express Card and the Amazon Business Prime American Express Card. These cards aim to help SMEs with cashflow by offering reward points or extended payment terms, especially relevant during the economic slowdown caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The initiative mirrors a successful collaboration between the two companies in the United States.

title: Lowe's plans large distribution center in Kyle
summary: Lowe's Cos. Inc. has leased 120,000 square feet at Kyle Crossing Business Park for a new distribution center. This move follows Amazon's existing lease of over 300,000 square feet in the same park, developed by Majestic Realty Co., hinting at more large projects for the developer in the Austin area.

title: When sports and financial markets collide
summary: The article discusses the increasing intersection of sports and financial markets, driven largely by the legalization of sports betting. It highlights the launch of sports betting and esports ETFs by Roundhill Investments and introduces the JohnWallStreet Sports Stock Index by Sportico, which tracks the growth of the domestic sports industry through 40 publicly traded companies.
